privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: This text describes the data processed by the Nocido Delivery app and the back office that goes with it, why it is processed, and what you can do about it.

who.title: Who processes your data
who.body: Nocido publishes the platform. The carrier that issued your account, the one whose name you entered when you first opened the app, is responsible for its own business data; Nocido hosts and processes it on their behalf, and makes no other use of it.

collected.title: What the app collects
collected.body: Your professional identity (last name, first name, phone, agency, city) and your sign-in credentials. The parcels you scan or create, the statuses, the amounts collected, your remittances, statements and invoices. The photos you take as proof of delivery, a cheque image or a claim attachment. A GPS point, only at the moment you confirm a delivery, and only if you granted the permission. And, if you accept notifications, a technical token identifying your installation of the app.

why.title: Why
why.body: To carry out delivery work: knowing which parcel is with whom, proving a handover, computing a commission, reconciling a payment. There is no other purpose: no profiling, no individual performance metrics sold on, no advertising.

not.title: What the app does not do
not.body: No advertising trackers, no cross-app tracking identifier, no ATT tracking prompt on iOS. Your location is never read in the background: the app does not request that permission and explicitly blocks it. No data is sold or handed to a third party for commercial purposes.

photos.title: Photos
photos.body: They are compressed on the phone before upload, and their EXIF metadata, including the device's GPS coordinates, is stripped at capture. They are attached to the parcel or statement they document, and visible only to authorised people at your carrier.

keeping.title: How long
keeping.body: Delivery data and accounting records are kept for as long as accounting and tax law requires. Technical logs are purged after twelve months. The notification token lives as long as the installation does: it goes when you sign out, when you uninstall, or as soon as the system tells us it is invalid. The app's cache is cleared from your device when you sign out.

shared.title: Who has access
shared.body: Authorised people at your carrier, according to the permissions their company granted them. Our hosting provider, solely to run the service. Expo's notification service, then Apple or Google, to deliver the notifications you accepted. A public authority, if it requests it in the form the law provides.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: Access, rectification, objection, restriction, portability. You can delete your account from the app, under Profile: your identity is then anonymised and your credentials stop working. Deliveries already carried out remain in your carrier's accounting history, with no link to your name, because the law requires them to keep those.

security.title: Security
security.body: All exchanges use HTTPS only. Your session tokens are kept in the phone's system vault (iOS Keychain, Android Keystore), never in the app's code. An optional biometric lock can be enabled under Profile. No personal data is written to technical logs.

complaint.title: Complaints
complaint.body: If an answer does not satisfy you, you may refer the matter to the Moroccan data protection authority (CNDP).

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: If you accept them, your device receives a technical token that we keep so we know where to send a message. The token says nothing about you: it identifies an installation of the app, not a person. We keep the platform, the device language and the installed version alongside it, so notifications are written in your language. Messages travel through Expo's notification service, then through Apple or Google depending on your phone; they never carry a recipient's name, phone or address, only a parcel or document code. The token is deleted when you sign out, when you uninstall the app, and when the system tells us it is no longer valid.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: These terms govern the use of the Nocido Delivery app. By using it, you accept them.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.body: The app lets a courier build their run by scanning, report the outcome of each job, review their remittances and statements, and submit a photo of their cheque.

access.title: Who may use it
access.body: It is for people to whom a Nocido customer carrier has issued an account. It is not open to public sign-up: without an account from your company, there is nothing to see.

account.title: Your account
account.body: Your credentials are personal. Whatever is done with your account is attributed to you: do not lend it, and report any use you do not recognise to your agency without delay.

use.title: Expected use
use.body: Report only what you actually observed. A status declared without the matching action distorts a payment, a commission and an invoice. Do not attempt to bypass the app's checks or to reach data unrelated to your own jobs.

record.title: What counts as the record
record.body: Events recorded on the server are authoritative between you and your carrier: timestamp, status, amount, photo. Where a queued action is replayed late, the last event received prevails.

offline.title: Offline and availability
offline.body: The app works without network: your actions go into a queue and are sent as soon as coverage returns. A banner tells you what has not gone out yet. We do not guarantee uninterrupted availability, nor the absence of maintenance downtime.

version.title: Updates
version.body: The app checks at launch that it is not too old. A version that has become incompatible with the service will ask you to update before continuing.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.body: Camera, "while using the app" location and photo access are requested when they are needed, never at launch. The app remains usable if you refuse them: only the features that depend on them are unavailable.

end.title: End of access
end.body: Your carrier may deactivate your account, in particular when your collaboration ends. You may delete your own under Profile. In both cases the company's accounting history is kept, with no link to your identity.

law.title: Governing law
law.body: These terms are governed by Moroccan law. Disputes fall to the competent courts of Casablanca.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: Notifications are a convenience, not a guarantee. They depend on Apple's and Google's services, on your network and on your phone's settings: a notification may arrive late, or not at all. They therefore never replace opening the app, and no deadline runs from the moment you receive one. You enable them by accepting the system prompt, and you choose what you receive, topic by topic, under Profile. Two topics cannot be turned off because they carry your work: a run being assigned to a courier, and a reply to a claim.
